families.family: brazil-first-phase (Primeira Fase da Maratona SBC / 'Sub-Regional Brasil do ICPC')

facts.participants: Brazil-only official division: 799 teams/196 schools (2020, online), 556/170 at 42 sedes (2022), 726/181 at 44 sedes (2023), 880/226 at 48 sedes (2024), 1025/239 at 53 sedes (2025), 965/233 at 54 sedes (2026) — consistent with the archive's median 641. A parallel unofficial online 'cafe com leite' division exists (26 BR teams 2025).
facts.problemset: Unique NEW problems every year, authored by the SBC committee (2025 selection committee: Arthur Nascimento, Mauricio Collares, Ricardo Anido, Vinicius dos Santos), 12-14 problems, Portuguese (recently + English). Official statements PDFs are titled 'Maratona de Programacao da SBC YYYY — Sub-Regional Brasil do ICPC'. Since 2021 this SAME set is exported to the Spanish-American September qualifiers (see sharing_matrix): GPMX 3ra fecha, GP Centroamerica, Bolivia Preliminary/CBP, TAP (2021-2022 only), Torneo Chileno (2023 only). It is NOT the November regional set and NOT shared with Colombia's Maraton Nacional.
facts.qualification: Sole gate into the Fase Nacional/Final da Maratona (= the archive's brazil series): ~65-66 teams advance under 4 published vaga rules (score rank, institution rank, underrepresented-institution/state slots, host slot). The Final Nacional is Brazil's ICPC regional (Joao Pessoa 2024, FECAP Sao Paulo 2025), which since the 2023-24 cycle feeds the ICPC Latin America Championship 'Programadores da America' (Salvador Mar 2025, Santiago Mar 2026) and thence the World Finals (6 BR teams to Dubai 2026).
facts.format: Same-day multi-site ONSITE at 42-54 university sedes across all 5 Brazilian regions (2026: 54 sedes in 26 states). COVID exception: 2020 First Phase held online (Nov 14, 2020) and the 2020 Final was postponed and held online (reported Jul 9-10, streamed); 2021 (Oct 30) was still a COVID-era edition. Onsite again from 2022 (one sede, Vitoria 2022, ran an online makeup after a power outage).
facts.host: Sociedade Brasileira de Computacao (SBC); site maratona.sbc.org.br; BOCA scoreboards/statements on scorelatam.naquadah.com.br (subbr-YYYY).

for: R1 pass: 170-240 institutions, every Brazilian state — the largest contest in Latin America.
R2 pass: unique new SBC problemset — it is the SOURCE set that four other countries' qualifiers import.
R3 pass: the only gate into the Fase Nacional -> LAC -> WF chain.
R4 pass: multi-site onsite by design; online only in COVID 2020(-21).
Own ICPC round identity: registered and titled 'Sub-Regional Brasil do ICPC', not merely an internal phase.
against: Identity lens: it is literally named 'Primeira Fase da Maratona SBC' — same geography (all Brazil) as the parent brazil series (Fase Nacional), so a strict reading folds it into the parent as an earlier round.

families.family: sa-joint-structure (South America-North & South America-South regionals vs the joint Latin America Regional)

facts.participants: SA/North sedes and per-year team counts 2008-2016: Colombia 38-41, Venezuela 15-32, Ecuador 2 (2008-09 only), Panama 3-8 (2014-16). SA/South: Argentina (Buenos Aires site also hosting Uruguay/Paraguay guests), Bolivia, Chile, Peru. 2024-25 sites: SA/N = Bogota + Caracas; SA/S = Buenos Aires, Tarija, Coquimbo, Arequipa + Lima.
facts.problemset: ONE synchronized problemset for the whole regional layer: 'since 2009 all ACM-ICPC regional contests in Latin America and the Caribbean compete the same day with the same problem set' (icpccaribe history), reaffirmed by the official LAR 2024-25 rules ('It occurs at the same date and time in each region (synchronized). Participating teams at each site receive the same problem set') covering Brazil, Caribbean, Central America, Mexico, SA/North, SA/South. Mirrored on Codeforces as the 'Latin American Regional Contests' gyms (2024-25 = gym 105505).
facts.qualification: SA-North and SA-South are per-subregion rankings/series of that joint contest; national qualifiers (Maraton Nacional CO, TAP, TCP, Competencia Boliviana, GPMX->Final Mexicana, GPCA, Caribbean eliminatoria) decide who sits at each country's site. Since the 2023-24 cycle the regionals promote ~40 teams (max 2/school) to the ICPC Latin America Championship, which selects the WF teams.
facts.format: Onsite at national sedes, one Saturday in Oct/Nov (Nov 9 2019, Oct 21 2023, Nov 9 2024, Nov 7 2026). Maratona Linux mandated at all sites (2024-25 rules).
facts.host: ICPC Latin America (icpclatam.org); history 1996-2003 one joint 'South America' regional including Brazil; 2004-2007 'Sudamerica (sin Brasil)' with Brazil as a separate series; 2008 split into SA/Norte and SA/Sur; 2009+ everything same-day/same-set.

for: This is exactly the maintainer's 'one joint contest, per-country/subregion rankings' — but it lives at the REGIONAL layer, not the national layer.
Both subregional series gate the WF path (regional -> LAC -> WF); the per-subregion split is how slots are allocated.
evidence: https://icpc.com.ar/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/icpc-latin-america-regionals-rules-2024-2025.pdf (six regionals, synchronized same-set, sites incl. Tarija/Coquimbo/Arequipa-Lima under SA/South and Bogota/Caracas under SA/North, ~40 to Championship)

https://www.icpccaribe.org/icpc-latam/concursos-regionales-acm-icpc-de-sudam%C3%A9rica-1996-2003 (joint SA regional 1996-2003 incl. Brazil; sibling pages for 2004-2007 sin Brasil, Brasil 2004-2016, Mexico y Centroamerica 1997-2016)

Judging on an online-judge environment per sede ('BOCA, PC2 o Kattis segun lo determine la sede' per current instructions); RPC (Red de Programacion Competitiva) provides the historical BOCA scoreboard infrastructure; problem-author identity not confirmed.
facts.qualification: Official ICPC qualifier: 'clasificatorio para representar a Colombia en las fases regionales y mundiales del ICPC' — it selects the Colombian teams for the SA/North regional (Bogota site; Colombia historically fields ~38-41 teams there), which feeds LAC -> WF.
facts.format: '100% presencial' — same-day multi-city onsite (6-8 sedes across Colombia); one Saturday Sep/Oct (Oct 19 2024, Sep 17 2022). COVID 2020-21 modality unverified (editions took place; results pages exist).
facts.host: ACIS (Asociacion Colombiana de Informatica) + REDIS; acis.org.co (per-year results pages catalogued in r2 groundwork); icpc.global finder ColombiaMaratonNalACISREDIS-2018..2027.

for: R1 pass (46+ institutions nationwide), R2 pass (own new problems, no sharing found), R3 pass (gates the SA/North seats for Colombia), R4 pass (multi-city onsite, explicitly '100% presencial').
against: Problem authorship and exact advance-quota rules not pinned down (acis.org.co non-www is robots/timeout-blocked through the fetch proxy; www.acis.org.co works for some pages).

facts.participants: 2019: 110 teams, 30 institutions, 12 sedes; 2022: 11 sedes; 2026: 14 confirmed sedes (Bariloche, Cordoba, Rosario, La Plata, etc.).
facts.problemset: Own AAPC problemset (problem PDFs 2013-2025; judges: SPOJ 2011-2015, Codeforces group YjFmW2O15Q 2016-2022, public CF gyms 104603/105321/106054 2023-2025) — EXCEPT 2021 and 2022, when TAP ran on the Brazilian SBC Sub-Regional set (named in the subbr-2021/subbr-2022 statements PDFs; TAP 2022 = Oct 8 2022, same day as Brazil, 87 Argentine teams counted on the Brazilian page), and 2019, when UNLP billed the edition as the joint 'Torneo Chileno-Argentino de Programacion' (11 shared problems with Chile's TCP).
facts.qualification: Gates Argentina's seats at the SA/South regional (Buenos Aires site): reglamento TAP 2026 promotes 55 teams to the Regional Latinoamericana of Nov 7 2026 (top-20 + per-institution + ranking + all-women reserved slots). Historically softer: in 2022-2023 institutions 'could (not mandatory) use the TAP to select teams' for the regional.
facts.format: ONSITE, simultaneous multi-sede across Argentina (9-14 university sedes; one computer per team, internet restricted to the judge URL). Held every year 2011-2026 (16th = Aug 29, 2026; predecessor 'Local UBA 2007'); COVID editions 2020-2021 took place (CF group judges exist) — remote modality likely but unverified.
facts.host: Asociacion Argentina de Programacion Competitiva (aapc.org.ar, ex icpc.com.ar / torneoprogramacion.com.ar); historical general coordination Pablo Heiber.

for: R1 pass (30 institutions/12+ cities), R2 pass with documented exceptions (own set except 2019 joint w/ Chile and 2021-22 SBC-shared — exactly the kind of sharing the maintainer wants recorded), R3 pass (formal 55-team gate to SA/South by 2026; selective role earlier), R4 pass (onsite multi-sede).

facts.participants: Large national funnels: 3ra fecha 2022 = 623 Mexican teams, 2025 = 265, 2026 = 670 (counts recorded on the Brazilian First-Phase pages). Qualifies 57-70 teams to the Final Mexicana (60 slots 2020 & 2021; 70 in 2026 with performance, IPN/host, all-women, state, community and repechaje slots).
facts.problemset: Own new problems per fecha (Mexican community/ITESO), EXCEPT the Tercera Fecha which since 2021 is the Brazilian SBC Sub-Regional set ('en conjunto con Primera Fase de region Brasil', ITESO 2026; subbr PDFs 2021-2024 name 'Tercera Fecha Gran Premio de Mexico').
facts.qualification: Cumulative standing over 3 fechas + repechaje gates the Final Mexicana / Eliminatoria Regional (Mexico's ICPC regional: Monterrey was the 2024 LAR site; ESCOM-IPN Nov 6-7 2026), which promotes to the Latin America Championship (formalized for the 2023-24 cycle) and the World Finals. Chain per Reglas ICPCMX2025: Gran Premio -> Final Mexicana -> Campeonato Regional LATAM -> Final Mundial.
facts.format: DISTRIBUTED ONSITE by rule, not an open online series: the official 2015 sede manual requires qualifying contests to run 'distribuido' with teams physically at registered university sedes under a Director de Sede; ITESO publishes 'convocatoria a sedes' yearly (2015, 2018) and the 2026 fechas are explicitly 'Presencial distribuido' (BOCA for fechas 1-2 and repechaje, MOJ for the Brazil-joint 3ra). Judging platforms churned: PC2 -> BOCA/COJ (2015) -> omegaUp arenas (~2019-2022, e.g. ICPCMX2022_1er) -> CF gyms (2023-2025: 105164/105216/105408, 105873/105979) -> BOCA/MOJ (2026). COVID: the 2020 Eliminatoria was postponed to Jul 10 2021 with an online/hybrid scheme under LATAM review, and the 2021 Eliminatoria was restructured to 'presencial distribuido en 7 sedes'; fecha modality in 2020-2022 leaned remote (unverified detail).
facts.host: ICPC Mexico community coordinated from ITESO (eventos.iteso.mx/acm hub, all years 2015-2026); 2015-2017 the event was the joint 'Gran Premio de Mexico y Centroamerica' (Mexico + Belize/Guatemala/Honduras/El Salvador/Nicaragua/Costa Rica), Mexico-only since 2018; finder slugs mcapgp-YYYY.

for: R1 pass (hundreds of teams, dozens of institutions and states), R3 pass (sole gate to the Final Mexicana chain), R4 pass under the maintainer's 'multi-site onsite counts as onsite' rule (sede model is mandated in the official manual and explicit again in 2026), R2 mostly pass (own fechas; the borrowed 3ra fecha is documented sharing, not duplication).
against: It is a SERIES of 3-4 dated rounds with cumulative standings rather than one contest — archive should model fechas as rounds of one yearly entry.
2020-2023 fecha modality (sede-proctored vs remote) is the weakest-documented stretch; omegaUp/CF-gym era invites an 'online series' reading if the sede convocatorias are ignored.
evidence: https://acm.iteso.mx/share/manual_sede_20150827.pdf (sede = physical university venue; 'los concursos que son clasificatorios tienen que organizarse en este formato [distribuido]'; countries MX+BZ/GT/HN/SV/NI/CR; PC2->BOCA/COJ; Gran Premio Jan-Oct -> Eliminatoria Regional 2nd weekend of November)

facts.participants: 2025: 95 teams (Costa Rica 31, Guatemala 36, El Salvador 28); 2026: 124 teams (CR 42, GT 60, SV 20, NI 2). Registration free, open to active university students of Guatemala, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica (2026); teams counted on the Brazil-set fecha: 11 (2022), 26 (2025), 120 (2026).
facts.problemset: Series of 4 fechas + repechaje with per-country and per-university breakdowns; at least one fecha each year 2021-2026 is the Brazilian SBC Sub-Regional set ('Tercera Fecha Gran Premio de Centroamerica 2021', 'Gran Premio de Centroamerica 2022/2023', 'The 2024 ICPC Gran Premio de Centroamerica' named in the subbr PDFs); other fechas presumably own/community problems (unverified).
facts.qualification: Cumulative standings select the teams for Central America's sites of the joint Latin America Regional (2024-25 LAR sites: Alajuela CR, San Salvador SV, Guatemala City GT) -> Latin America Championship -> WF. The 2026 results are marked 'no oficiales' pending the finals.
facts.format: Inherited the distributed-sede model of the joint 2015-2017 'Gran Premio de Mexico y Centroamerica' (the 2015 sede manual covered Belize/Guatemala/Honduras/El Salvador/Nicaragua/Costa Rica sedes and mandated distributed presencial for qualifiers). families.family: bolivia (Competencia Nacional / Bolivia Preliminary / Competencia Boliviana de Programacion)

facts.participants: On the shared September contest: 116 teams (2022), 197 (2025), 227 (2026). The separate 'Pre-National' Codeforces gym 105230 (2024-25 season) shows 81+ teams, 11 problems A-K.
facts.problemset: The official national qualifier ('The 2022/2023 ICPC Bolivia Preliminary Contest', renamed 'Competencia Boliviana de Programacion' from 2024) has NEVER had its own problemset in the located era: every year 2022-2026 it is the Brazilian SBC Sub-Regional set, sat simultaneously with Brazil/Mexico/Central America. A separate Bolivian-organized 'Pre-National Contest' (CF gym, e.g. Sep 3 2024) runs shortly before as a warm-up/seeding round with its own problems.
facts.qualification: Gates Bolivia's site of the SA/South joint regional (Tarija in 2024-25; Bolivia has fielded joint-regional sedes since 2003) -> LAC -> WF.
facts.format: Same-day-as-Brazil September contest; Bolivian teams presumably sit at university sedes (the SBC contest is sede-based and Bolivia hosts LAR sedes onsite), but Bolivian-side proctoring was not directly verified; the Pre-National gym round is online-flavored (public CF gym + vjudge mirrors).
facts.host: ICPC Bolivia community (icpc-bolivia.edu.bo — dead/unresolvable through the proxy; active Facebook 'icpc.bolivia.oficial'); finder Bolivia-Preliminary-2023/-2025/-2026 + current alias.

for: R1 pass (multiple universities: UMSS, UCB, UPB, UMSA etc.; 100-227 teams), R3 pass (the split ranking is what seats Bolivian teams at Tarija/SA-South), maintainer's rule: joint same-day shared-set contests are acceptable when the split gates qualification — which is exactly Bolivia's situation.
R4 leaning pass: part of the same-day multi-site onsite September event.

Onsite proctoring in Bolivia not directly evidenced.

facts.participants: Venezuela sede of the SA/North joint regional: 23/20/15/21/19/16/32/24/17 teams in 2008-2016 (icpccaribe history); recent editions smaller (standings exist in the finder for 2018-19, 2022, 2024, 2025).

sharing_matrix: TWO distinct sharing layers exist, and the maintainer's 'one joint contest with per-country rankings' belief is true at BOTH — but with different membership. (A) REGIONAL layer (November, 'Latin America Regional'): since 2009 every ICPC regional contest in Latin America and the Caribbean runs on the same day with the same problemset (icpccaribe history; LAR 2024-25 rules 'synchronized... same problem set'; the CF 'Latin American Regional Contests' gyms). The archive's South America-North series (Colombia+Venezuela sedes, +Ecuador 2008-09 & 2022, +Panama 2014-16), South America-South series (Argentina w/ UY-PY guests, Bolivia, Chile, Peru), brazil series (Final Nacional da Maratona = the Brazil sites), Mexico Finals/Final Mexicana, the Central America sites, and the Caribbean Finals are all per-subregion/per-country ranked instances of that one synchronized contest. 'Venezuela Finals' (2011-2025) and 'Ecuador Finals' (2022) are, on all located evidence, precisely per-country cuts of this joint regional — NOT separate national contests. Historical arc: 1996-2003 one joint South America regional incl. Brazil; 2004-2007 'Sudamerica (sin Brasil)' joint + separate Brazil regional; 2008 SA split into Norte/Sur; 2009+ full LatAm+Caribbean synchronization; since the 2023-24 cycle the regionals feed the Latin America Championship ('Programadores de America') which picks the WF teams. (B) NATIONAL/first-phase layer (Aug-Oct): the Brazilian SBC Primeira Fase problemset ('Sub-Regional Brasil do ICPC', authored by SBC) became the shared set of a September joint block, with per-country contests and rankings: 2021 (Oct 30) Brazil + Gran Premio de Mexico 3ra Fecha + Gran Premio de Centroamerica 3ra Fecha + Torneo Argentino de Programacion; 2022 (Oct 8) those four + Bolivia Preliminary (TAP's last year on it — TAP 2022 same day, 87 AR teams); 2023 (Sep 2) Brazil + GPMX 3ra + GPCA + Bolivia + Torneo Chileno (Chile's only year; Argentina back on its own set); 2024 (Aug 31) Brazil + GPMX + GPCA + Competencia Boliviana; 2025 (Sep 13) Brazil (1025 teams) + Bolivia (197) + Mexico (265) + CA (26); 2026 (Aug 29) Brazil (965) + Bolivia (227) + Mexico (670, 'presencial distribuido en conjunto con Primera Fase de region Brasil') + CA (120). Within this block only ONE of Mexico's/CA's 3-4 fechas is shared (the tercera); their other fechas are own problems, while Bolivia's entire national qualifier IS the shared contest (it has never had its own set, 2022-2026). Other national-layer sharing: TAP & TCP ran 2019 as one joint 'Torneo Chileno-Argentino de Programacion' (same 11 problems; UNLP headline); Gran Premio de Mexico y Centroamerica was literally one event 2015-2017 before splitting in 2018; the Caribbean CNC (2011-2019) was per-country simultaneous contests on one shared Caribbean set, merged 2020+ into the single online CFQ. NOT shared, contrary to the maintainer's suspicion: Colombia's Maraton Nacional ACIS/REDIS — own problems, own date (e.g. Sep 17 2022 vs the block's Oct 8; Oct 19 2024 vs Aug 31), Colombia-only, never named in any subbr PDF; TAP from 2023 on (own AAPC set, e.g. Sep 16 2023); TCP in 2024-2025 (own SCPC set, Oct 4-5); and the Caribbean sets are independent of the continental blocks. The RPC (Red de Programacion Competitiva) runs a separate biweekly multi-country training circuit (10+ countries, 250+ institutions) and supplies BOCA infrastructure, but its circuit rounds are not the national qualifiers.
